neighbours.label: A perfect auxiliary (has, have, had) in an 'after' or 'once' clause, marking an event as completed before what follows, versus the same words in clauses of cause, condition or possession
fire: Compost the peelings after they have gone soft, instead of throwing them in the bin.
Most people discard the jars after these have served a single use.
Once the waiting period has expired, the tenants can apply again.
After the volcano had covered the valley in ash, the harvests failed for years.
After the flood had receded, the villagers came back to clean their homes.
Replace the filter once it has reached the end of its useful life.
Once the treaty had been signed, the troops started to withdraw.
Drain the pasta after it has boiled for nine minutes, and add the sauce.
quiet: Compost the peelings because they have plenty of nutrients, instead of throwing them in the bin.
Most people keep the jars since these have sturdy lids and wide mouths.
While the waiting period is running, the tenants have to stay in the building.
The volcano had a wide crater, and the valley has rich soil to this day.
During the flood the villagers came back to clean their homes and feed animals.
Replace the filter if it has a crack or a bad smell.
Before the treaty had any force, the troops started to withdraw.
Drain the pasta when it is soft enough, and add the sauce.
